data.hypothesis: The measured baseline is 0.4575 s, the selected hybrid parent is 0.2396 s, the prior all-per-timestep candidate is 0.2376 s, and the catalog best is 0.2292 s. These aggregate results do not isolate region lifetime by thread budget. This candidate reverses the parent's dispatch for larger work: one thread uses a persistent team, while larger budgets create a region per timestep. That tests whether avoiding repeated single-thread region launches helps at one core and whether repeated regions matter at four cores; small work stays serial. No speedup is assumed.
data.notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is changed. No commands, builds, or local correctness/performance checks were run. The controller should verify full output, boundaries, smaller cases, and n=256, then measure the official one- and four-core settings.
transformations: Retained the serial stencil, initialization, six-step ping-pong behavior, and serial path for small work or nonpositive thread budgets.
Kept static row-level OpenMP scheduling and the call-specific num_threads budget without changing global OpenMP state.

For larger work, selected one persistent region at a one-thread budget and one parallel region per timestep at larger budgets, reversing the selected parent's mapping to contrast region lifetime at the official settings.
Kept SIMD and temporal blocking out of scope.
